Ravi: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands Q&A thread. A few targeted questions so teams can act: 1) How should engineering orgs position Redwood vs major cloud AI endpoints when customers ask about lock-in? 2) For product-led cohorts, what signals should trigger an outbound to propose Dedicated? 3) Are we shifting any regional prioritization for Private (EU/APAC)? 4) Any immediate changes to standard discounting or commit buckets? 5) Where does safety & compliance sit in the roadmap for hosted features?

Lina: Great set of asks. TL;DR: position = "owner of serving" not model ownership. Our defensible play is operational primitives (routing, KV + prefix caching, model variant fallback, deterministic perf profiles) + transparent unit economics. That reduces customer risk of surprise costs and gives predictable SLAs.

Diego: To add color for eng teams: show them side-by-side perf/cost comparisons on realistic workloads (small chat app, high-throughput embedding pipeline). Emphasize batch-aware kernel selection and runtime caching. Those are engineering differentiators customers notice in latency and cost per million tokens.

Harper: Hosted -> Dedicated signals: sustained >90 days of steady token volume, repeated rate-limit escalations, strict latency SLOs (p95 < 250ms), or compliance requirements. Playbook: offer a 60-day pilot with reserved capacity and an optional performance tuning session.

Maya: Sales note: for PLG users, trigger when they cross both spend and latency signals (e.g., $X/month + >Y concurrent qps). We should automate a lead-gen flag in the console for these customers. Revenue Ops to own thresholds.

Ravi: Regions question? We heard EU priority at all-hands, any nuance?

Lina: EU still first for Private (GDPR + enterprise pipeline). APAC is second wave; we'll prioritize cloud-region availability first, then channel partners for on-prem pilots. For regulated verticals we fast-track Private regardless of region.

Diego: Technical note: Private deployments will ship with a default KMS integration and audit log pipes. Ops/security teams will get a hardened config by default.

Harper: Pricing/discounts: no immediate change to the canonical commit buckets. But we're standardizing a clearer discount matrix tied to committed throughput and multi-year terms. For now, use existing tiers and loop in RevOps for exceptions.

Maya: Also recommending a customer-facing one-pager that maps commit tiers to expected p50/p95 latency and cost per token. Will collaborate with Product Marketing.

Ravi: Safety: what should hosted customers expect vs Private?

Lina: Hosted includes baseline content filtering, telemetry for prompt-level anomalies, and our standard incident response SLAs. Private gets optional local policies, full KMS control, and more granular audit retention. We're also adding release gates: model rollouts require passing eval suites before promoting from canary.

Diego: We'll expose a "release checklist" endpoint and a small curl example for teams to integrate with CI. Example: `curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer CI_TOKEN' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/releases/checklist -d '{"model":"redwood-7b", "eval_set":"chat-smoke"}'`

Ravi: Two asks: 1) Can leadership publish a short positioning blurb for proposals? 2) Can Product ship the Hosted->Dedicated migration kit and the perf/cost spreadsheet?

Lina: Yes to both. We'll publish a 100-150 word positioning blurb focused on predictable inference economics, unified runtime across deployment modes, and production guardrails. Product will own the migration kit and will deliver the perf/cost spreadsheet next week.

Diego: Noted 44d I'll add the demo script and a small read-only metrics endpoint in the runtime for product to hook into.

Lina: Thanks all 44f keep the follow-ups coming in #all-hands-questions.
